picks.title: Iron Age Ireland
picks.summary:
How much of Iron Age Ireland is myth, and how much is archaeological reality? At the monumental Hill of Tara, sacred kings ruled over a landscape steeped in ancient ritual and ancestral memory.


Tristan Hughes is joined by Dr. John Waddell, author of The Celtic World, to explore the truth to be found through the mist and beneath the hills. We hear about legendary rulers like Queen Medb, epic cattle raids, massive ceremonial feasts, and lawless, roaming war bands.


MORE

Iron Age Britain
picks.reason: Examines Irish Iron Age myths and their archaeological and cultural significance.

picks.title: Emily Wilson on CROSSING THE WINE-DARK SEA
picks.summary: Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea by Emily Wilson takes readers on a tour through the ancient world for an entertaining examination of Greek and Roman literature and their impact on our modern world. Emily joins us to talk about the joys and challenges of interpreting antiquity, the stakes of poetic form and re-translating The Odyssey with cohost Jenna Seery. This episode of Poured Over was hosted by Jenna Seery and mixed by Harry Liang. New episodes land Tuesdays and Thursdays (with occasional Saturdays) here and on your favorite podcast app. Featured Books:  Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea by Emily Wils
picks.reason: Discusses ancient Greek and Roman literature and its modern cultural impact.

picks.summary: We grew up with stories of tiny winged creatures, sparkling forests, magical wishes, and gentle fairies who helped lost travelers. Why were they feared as much as they were admired? picks.reason: Explores the darker, original folklore of fairies beyond modern portrayals.

picks.summary: Cliff Barackman and Matt Pruitt speak with folklorist Dr. Lynne McNeill about the intersection of folklore, science, and the sasquatch! Dr. McNeill is an Associate Professor of Folklore at Utah State University. Her research focuses on legend and belief, cryptids, digital culture, and the ways that folklore develops and spreads through communities. Dr. McNeill discusses what folklore actually is, why folklorists study it, and what traditional stories tell us about the world around us.
